title: Regional headroom querysheet — post-incident data pull
content:
SUMMARY:
This sheet contains the raw query definitions, field list, pull parameters, and a compact CSV-style sample slice used during the August 28 — September 2 2026 capacity incident postmortem. Goal: produce a repeatable, auditable data extract that captures saturation, queueing, and throttle signals across regions and GPU families so the incident RCA can quantify where headroom assumptions were violated.

PURPOSE / AUDIENCE:
- For infra SREs and platform/serving teams to replay key metrics used in the postmortem.
- To serve as the canonical input for charts in the RCA doc and follow-up capacity planning.

TIME WINDOW:
- Incidence window: 2026-08-28 00:00 UTC through 2026-09-02 23:59 UTC (primary).
- Baseline window (for diff): 2026-07-24 00:00 UTC through 2026-07-30 23:59 UTC (same weekday pattern).

PULL PARAMETERS / FILTERS:
- Granularity: 1-min aggregates (primary), 5-min rollups for long-term trends.
- Include only production serving clusters (cluster_label IN ("prod-eu", "prod-us", "prod-apac")).
- Exclude warmup traffic (traffic_tag != 'canary' and request_latency_ms > 1).
- Join telemetry tables by request_id to get token_count and throttle_reason.

FIELDS (flat schema exported):
- event_ts_utc
- cluster
- region
- gpu_model
- instance_type
- alloc_id
- host_ip
- queued_requests_count
- avg_queue_ms
- p50_queue_ms
- p95_queue_ms
- gpu_util_pct
- gpu_mem_pct
- running_workloads
- available_gpus
- pending_evictions
- throttle_count
- throttle_reason_codes (comma-delimited)
- tokens_generated
- requests_per_minute
- avg_latency_ms
- kv_cache_hit_pct
- batch_size_avg
- seq_len_avg

NOTES ON METRICS:
- queued_requests_count reflects the number of requests in local per-host scheduling queue when the 1-min sample was taken. Some requests are split across lanes; we dedupe by request_id in the join.
- gpu_util_pct is computed from driver-level counters and normalized to the device peak for model-profile used in production.
- throttle_count includes both soft throttle (enqueue backpressure) and hard throttle (HTTP 429). throttle_reason_codes are normalized to the THR_* taxonomy (THR_NO_CAPACITY, THR_REGION_LIMIT, THR_MODEL_LOCK, THR_CONFIG).

PRIMARY SQL (BigQuery style) USED FOR PULL:
-- NOTE: simplified for doc; actual job uses partitioned tables and service account
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(t.event_ts, MINUTE) as event_ts_utc,
  t.cluster, t.region, s.gpu_model, s.instance_type, s.alloc_id, s.host_ip,
  SUM(t.queued_count) as queued_requests_count,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(t.queue_ms, 100)[OFFSET(50)] as p50_queue_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(t.queue_ms, 20)[OFFSET(19)] as p95_queue_ms,
  AVG(s.gpu_util_pct) as gpu_util_pct,
  AVG(s.gpu_mem_pct) as gpu_mem_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.workload_id) as running_workloads,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.state='available' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as available_gpus,
  SUM(t.throttled) as throttle_count,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT t.throttle_reason, ',') as throttle_reason_codes,
  SUM(t.tokens) as tokens_generated,
  SUM(t.requests)/60 as requests_per_minute,
  AVG(t.latency_ms) as avg_latency_ms,
  AVG(s.kv_cache_hit_pct) as kv_cache_hit_pct,
  AVG(t.batch_size) as batch_size_avg,
  AVG(t.seq_len) as seq_len_avg
FROM telemetry.request_queue_samples t
JOIN telemetry.host_state s ON t.host_id = s.host_id AND TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(t.event_ts, MINUTE) = TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(s.sample_ts, MINUTE)
WHERE t.event_ts BETWEEN '2026-08-28' AND '2026-09-02'
  AND t.cluster IN ('prod-us','prod-eu','prod-apac')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
ORDER BY event_ts_utc ASC

KEY OBSERVATIONS (from this extract):
- Hot spots were concentrated in us-west1 (prod-us) and asia-southeast1 (prod-apac) with sustained queue p95 > 300ms and device util > 98% for multi-hour stretches.
- Several hosts show repeated high pending_evictions and zero available_gpus despite autoscaler signals; points to allocation throttles at the scheduler layer rather than hardware shortage in some microcases.
- Throttle taxonomy indicates ~72% of recorded throttles map to THR_NO_CAPACITY, ~18% THR_REGION_LIMIT, ~7% THR_MODEL_LOCK, rest are misc.
- Average kv_cache_hit_pct dropped 20-35 percentage points in affected regions starting 2026-08-29 10:00 UTC; this correlates with larger avg_latency_ms and higher token churn (tokens_generated per minute spiked).

ANOMALY DETECTION CHECKS RUN WITH THE PULL:
- 3-sigma anomaly on requests_per_minute per cluster by minute (flag rows where rps > baseline_mu + 3*sigma).
- detect runs where p95_queue_ms increased > 5x baseline for >= 30 minutes.
- host-level sticky-throttle: host that reports throttle_count > 100 in a 1-hour window and same host has available_gpus=0 for > 6 consecutive samples.

FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS & SUGGESTED NEXT STEPS:
- Provide this extract to scheduling team (cc: @Grace Huang) with focus on hosts flagged by sticky-throttle.\n Add per-host heap/oom logs for the flagged times.
- Re-evaluate autoscaler headroom policy for us-west1 and asia-southeast1; recommended temporary uplift of reserve capacity by 15% in those regions during peak windows.
- Create a lightweight alert for kv_cache_hit_pct drop (>15% over 30m) tied to traffic patterns to reduce regression time in future.
- Add a reconciliation batch job that compares scheduler allocation decisions to host_state.available_gpus every 5 minutes for 48 hours after rollout of any scheduling change.

EXTRA NOTES ABOUT THIS PULL JOB:
- Job name: infra.capacity.pull.region_headroom.20260914
- Service account used: infra-datareader@redwood-inference.internal
- Estimated size: ~18M rows per 1-min granularity for the primary window; compressed CSV ~1.1GB.
- Retention in GCS: gs://infra-exports/capacity-postmortem/2026-09-region-headroom/ (exports retained 90 days).
